body.translated_text: <s>Vigrahavyāvartanī-kārikā</s> (Verses on the Turning Back of Objections)

children.text: sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ sarvatra na vidyate svabhāvaś cet |
children.translated_text: If the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of all things does not exist anywhere,

children.text: tvadvacanam asvabhāvaṃ na nivartayituṃ svabhāvam alam || NagVvy_01
children.translated_text: then your statement, being without <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), is unable to negate <s>svabhāva</s>. // NagVvy_01

children.text: atha savabhāvam etad vākyaṃ pūrvā hatā pratijñā te |
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, this statement has <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), your former thesis is defeated.

children.text: vaiṣamikatvaṃ tasmin viśeṣahetuś ca vaktavyaḥ || NagVvy_02
children.translated_text: There is an inconsistency in that, and a special reason must be stated. // NagVvy_02

children.text: mā śabdavad ity etat syāt te buddhir na caitad upapannam |
children.translated_text: You might think, 'Let it be like sound' — but this is not tenable,

children.text: śabdena hy atra satā bhaviṣyato vāraṇaṃ tasya || NagVvy_03
children.translated_text: for it is by an existent sound that the prevention of that [future sound] will occur. // NagVvy_03

children.text: pratiṣedhapratiṣedho 'py evam iti mataṃ bhavet tad asad eva |
children.translated_text: 'The negation of negation also applies in the same way' — this view would be unfounded.

children.text: evaṃ tava pratijñā lakṣaṅato dūṣyate na mama || NagVvy_04
children.translated_text: Thus your thesis is refuted by its own defining characteristic, not mine. // NagVvy_04

children.text: pratyakṣeṇa hi tāvad yady upalabhya vinivartayasi bhāvān |
children.translated_text: If, to begin with, you negate things by apprehending them through <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception),

children.text: tan nāsti pratyakṣaṃ bhāvā yenopalabhyante || NagVvy_05
children.translated_text: then that <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) does not exist, by which things are apprehended. // NagVvy_05

children.text: anumānaṃ pratyuktaṃ pratyakṣeṇāgamopamāne ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is refuted along with <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception), as are <s>āgama</s> (scripture) and <s>upamāna</s> (analogy);

children.text: anumānāgamasādhyā ye 'rthā dṛṣṭāntasādhyāś ca || NagVvy_06
children.translated_text: the objects established by <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>āgama</s> (scripture), and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) [are also refuted]. // NagVvy_06

children.text: kuśalānāṃ dharmāvasthāvidaś ca manyante |
children.translated_text: Those who know the states of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) consider that the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature)

children.text: kuśalaṃ janāḥ svabhāvaṃ śeṣeṣv apy eṣa viniyogaḥ || NagVvy_07
children.translated_text: of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> is wholesome; this classification applies to the rest as well. // NagVvy_07

children.text: nairyāṇikasvabhāvo dharmā nairyāṇikāś ca ye teṣām |
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that are conducive to liberation have a nature conducive to liberation;

children.text: dharmāvasthoktānām evaṃ anairyāṇikādīnām || NagVvy_08
children.translated_text: thus it is for those <s>dharmas</s> described as states — and likewise for those not conducive to liberation, and so on. // NagVvy_08

children.text: yadi ca na bhavet svabhāvo dharmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāva ity evam |
children.translated_text: And if the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) does not exist, then the very name 'without svabhāva'

children.text: nāmāpi bhaven naivaṃ nāma hi nirvastukaṃ nāsti || NagVvy_09
children.translated_text: would not exist either, for a name without a referent does not exist. // NagVvy_09

children.text: atha vidyate svabhāvaḥ sa ca dharmāṇāṃ na vidyate tasmāt |
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) exists but does not belong to <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), then

children.text: dharmair vinā svabhāvaḥ sa yasya tad yuktam upadeṣṭum || NagVvy_10
children.translated_text: it is proper to teach that <s>svabhāva</s> belongs to something apart from <s>dharmas</s>. // NagVvy_10

children.text: sata eva pratiṣedho nāsti ghaṭo geha ity ayaṃ yasmāt |
children.translated_text: Negation is of what exists, since one sees the negation 'There is no pot in the house';

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ pratiṣedho 'yaṃ sataḥ svabhāvasya te tasmāt || NagVvy_11
children.translated_text: therefore, this negation of yours is of an existent <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). // NagVvy_11

children.text: atha nāsti sa svabhāvaḥ kiṃ nu pratiṣidhyate tvayānena |
children.translated_text: If, however, that <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) does not exist, what then is negated by you

children.text: vacanenarte vacanāt pratiṣedhaḥ sidhyate hy asataḥ || NagVvy_12
children.translated_text: with this statement? For the negation of the non-existent is accomplished without a statement. // NagVvy_12

children.text: bālānāṃ iva mithyā mṛgatṛṣnāyāṃ yathājalagrāhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the grasping of water in a mirage is false, as with children,

children.text: evaṃ mithyāgrāhaḥ syāt te pratiṣedhyato hy asataḥ || NagVvy_13
children.translated_text: so would your grasping be false, since what you negate is non-existent. // NagVvy_13

children.text: nanv evaṃ saty asti grāho grāhyaṃ ca tadgrahītā ca |
children.translated_text: But if it is so, then grasping exists, as does the graspable and the grasper,

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣeddhā ceti ṣaṭkaṃ tat || NagVvy_14
children.translated_text: negation, the negatable, and the negator — that makes a sixfold [set]. // NagVvy_14

children.text: atha naivāsti grāho naiva grāhyaṃ na ca grahītāraḥ |
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, there is no grasping, no graspable, and no graspers,

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣeddhāro nanu sa santi || NagVvy_15
children.translated_text: then negation, negatable, and negators — do they not also exist? // NagVvy_15

body.text: pratiṣedhaḥ pratiṣedhyaṃ pratiṣeddhāraś ca yadyuta na santi |
body.translated_text: If negation, negatable, and negators do not exist,

body.text: siddhā hi sarvabhāvās teṣam eva svabhāvaś ca || NagVvy_16
body.translated_text: then all things are established, along with their <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). // NagVvy_16

children.text: hetoś ca te na siddhir naiḥsvābhāvyāt kuto hi te hetuḥ |
children.translated_text: And your reason is not established, for from where comes your reason, given the absence of <s>svabhāva</s>?

children.text: nirhetukasya siddhir na copapannāsya te 'rthasya || NagVvy_17
children.translated_text: The establishment of your thesis without a reason is not tenable. // NagVvy_17

children.text: yadi cāhetoḥ siddhiḥ svabhāvavinivartanasya te bhavati |
children.translated_text: And if the establishment of the negation of <s>svabhāva</s> is accomplished without a cause,

children.text: svābhāvyasyāstitvaṃ mamāpi nirhetukaṃ siddham || NagVvy_18
children.translated_text: then the existence of <s>svabhāva</s> is also established for me without a cause. // NagVvy_18

children.text: atha hetor astitvaṃ bhāvāsvābhāvyam ity anupapannam |
children.translated_text: If existence is due to a cause, the lack of <s>svabhāva</s> in things is untenable,

children.text: lokeṣu niḥsvabhāvo na hi kaś cana vidyate bhāvaḥ || NagVvy_19
children.translated_text: for in the worlds there is not found any thing whatsoever that is without <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). // NagVvy_19

children.text: pūrvaṃ cet pratiṣedhaḥ paścāt pratiṣedhyam ity anupapannam |
children.translated_text: If the negation comes first and the negatable comes after, that is untenable;

children.text: paścāc cānupapanno yugapac ca yataḥ svabhāvaḥ san || NagVvy_20
children.translated_text: and it is untenable afterwards or simultaneously, because <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) [already] exists. // NagVvy_20

children.text: hetupratyayasāmagryāṃ ca pṛthak cāpi madvaco na yadi |
children.translated_text: If my statement does not arise from the assemblage of causes and conditions, nor separately,

children.text: manu śūnyatvaṃ siddhaṃ bhāvānām asvabhāvatvāt || NagVvy_21
children.translated_text: then <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is established, because things lack <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). // NagVvy_21

children.text: yaś ca pratītyabhāvo bhāvānāṃ śūnyateti sā proktā |
children.translated_text: The dependent arising of things — that is declared to be <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness);

children.text: yaś pratītyabhāvo bhavati hi tasyāsvabhāvatvam || NagVvy_22
children.translated_text: that which arises dependently, that indeed lacks <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). // NagVvy_22

children.text: nirmitako nirmitakaṃ māyāpuruṣaḥ svamāyayā sṛṣṭam |
children.translated_text: Just as a magically created being might negate another magically created being,

children.text: pratiṣedhayeta yadvat pratiṣedho 'yaṃ tathaiva syāt || NagVvy_23
children.translated_text: or a man created by magic might negate one created by his own magic — this negation would be just like that. // NagVvy_23

children.text: na svābhāvikam etad vākyaṃ tasmān na vādahānir me |
children.translated_text: This statement is not of intrinsic nature; therefore there is no loss of my argument.

children.text: nāsti ca vaiṣamikatvaṃ viśeṣahetuś ca na nigadyaḥ || NagVvy_24
children.translated_text: There is no inconsistency, and no special reason needs to be stated. // NagVvy_24

children.text: mā śabdavad iti nāyaṃ dṛṣṭānto yas tvayā samārabdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The example 'let it be like sound' that you have adduced is not applicable,

children.text: śabdena hi tac chabdasya vāraṇaṃ naivam etac ca || NagVvy_25
children.translated_text: for it is by sound that the prevention of [another] sound occurs, but this case is not like that. // NagVvy_25

children.text: naiḥsvābhāvyānāṃ cen naiḥsvābhāvyena vāraṇaṃ yadi hi |
children.translated_text: If the prevention of those without <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) is through the lack of <s>svabhāva</s>,

children.text: naiḥsvābhāvyanivṛttau svābhāvyaṃ hi prasiddhaṃ syāt || NagVvy_26
children.translated_text: then through the cessation of the lack of <s>svabhāva</s>, <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) would be established. // NagVvy_26

children.text: atha vā nirmitakāyāṃ yathā striyāṃ strīyam ity asadgrāham |
children.translated_text: Or, just as a magically created man might dispel the false apprehension

children.text: nirmitakaḥ pratihanyāt kasya cid evaṃ bhaved etat || NagVvy_27
children.translated_text: of 'she is a woman' regarding a magically created woman — so too could this be the case. // NagVvy_27

children.text: atha vā sādhyasamo 'yaṃ hetur na hi vidyate dhvaneḥ sattā |
children.translated_text: Or, this reason is equivalent to what is to be proved, for the existence of sound is not established;

children.text: saṃvyavahāraṃ ca vayaṃ nānabhyupagamya kathayāmaḥ || NagVvy_28
children.translated_text: and we do not speak without accepting conventional usage. // NagVvy_28

children.text: yadi kā cana pratijñā syān me tata eṣa me bhaved doṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: If I had any thesis whatsoever, then this fault would be mine;

children.text: nāsti ca mama pratijñā tasmān naivāsti me doṣaḥ || NagVvy_29
children.translated_text: but I have no thesis, therefore there is no fault of mine. // NagVvy_29

children.text: yadi kiṃ cid upalabheyaṃ pravartayeyaṃ nivartayeyaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: If I were to apprehend anything, I would either affirm or negate

children.text: pratyakṣādibhir arthais tadabhāvān me 'nupālambhaḥ || NagVvy_30
children.translated_text: through objects [known by] <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and the rest; since those are absent, I am without apprehension. // NagVvy_30

children.text: yadi ca pramāṇatas te teṣāṃ teṣāṃ prasiddhir arthānām |
children.translated_text: If the establishment of those various objects is through <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) for you,

children.text: teṣāṃ punaḥ prasiddhiṃ brūhi kathaṃ te pramāṇānām || NagVvy_31
children.translated_text: then tell how the establishment of those <s>pramāṇas</s> themselves occurs. // NagVvy_31

children.text: anyair yadi pramāṇaiḥ pramāṇasiddhir bhavet tad anavasthā |
children.translated_text: If the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) is through other <s>pramāṇas</s>, there is an infinite regress;

children.text: nādeḥ siddhis tatrāsti naiva madhyasya nāntasya || NagVvy_32
children.translated_text: in that case there is no establishment of the beginning, nor of the middle, nor of the end. // NagVvy_32

children.text: teṣām atha pramāṇair vinā prasiddhir vihīyate vādaḥ |
children.translated_text: If, however, their establishment is without <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), your argument is abandoned;

children.text: vaiṣamikatvaṃ tasmin viśeṣahetuś ca vaktavyaḥ || NagVvy_33
children.translated_text: there is an inconsistency in that, and a special reason must be stated. // NagVvy_33

children.text: viṣamopanyāso 'yaṃ na hy ātmānaṃ prakāśayaty agniḥ |
children.translated_text: This is an unequal comparison, for fire does not illuminate itself;

children.text: na hi tasyānupalabdhir dṛṣṭā tamasīva kumbhasya || NagVvy_34
children.translated_text: indeed, its non-apprehension in darkness has not been observed, as with a pot. // NagVvy_34

children.text: yadi ca svātmānam ayaṃ tvadvacanena prakāśayaty agniḥ |
children.translated_text: And if, according to your statement, this fire illuminates itself,

children.text: param iva nanv ātmānaṃ svaṃ paridhakṣyaty api hutāśaḥ || NagVvy_35
children.translated_text: then will not the fire also burn itself, just as it burns other things? // NagVvy_35

children.text: yadi ca svaparātmānau tvadvacanena prakāśayaty agniḥ |
children.translated_text: And if, according to your statement, fire illuminates both itself and others,

children.text: pracchādayiṣyati tamaḥ svaparātmānau hutāśa iva || NagVvy_36
children.translated_text: then darkness too should conceal both itself and others, just like fire. // NagVvy_36

children.text: nāsti tamaś ca jvalane yatra ca tiṣṭhati parātmani jvalanaḥ |
children.translated_text: There is no darkness in fire, nor in that other in which the fire abides;

children.text: kurute kathaṃ prakāśaṃ sa hi prakāśo 'ndhakāravadhaḥ || NagVvy_37
children.translated_text: how then does it produce illumination? For illumination is the destruction of darkness. // NagVvy_37

children.text: utpadyamāna eva prakāśayaty agnir ity asadvādaḥ |
children.translated_text: The claim that fire illuminates even while being born is untenable,

children.text: utpadyamāna eva prāpnoti tamo na hi hutāśaḥ || NagVvy_38
children.translated_text: for fire, even while being born, does not reach darkness. // NagVvy_38

children.text: aprāpto 'pi jvalano yadi vā punar andhakāram upahanyāt |
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, fire could destroy darkness even without reaching it,

children.text: sarveṣu lokadhātuṣu tamo 'yam iha saṃsthito hanyāt || NagVvy_39
children.translated_text: then this fire, stationed here, would destroy the darkness in all world-realms. // NagVvy_39

children.text: yadi svataś ca pramāṇasiddhir anapekṣya tava prameyāṇi |
children.translated_text: If the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) is self-derived, without depending on <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge),

children.text: bhavati pramāṇasiddhir na parāpekṣā svataḥsiddhiḥ || NagVvy_40
children.translated_text: then the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> is self-sufficient, not dependent on anything else. // NagVvy_40

children.text: anapekṣya hi prameyān arthān yadi te pramāṇasiddhir iti |
children.translated_text: If the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) is without depending on objects of knowledge,

children.text: na bhavanti kasya cid evam imāni tāni pramāṇāni || NagVvy_41
children.translated_text: then these <s>pramāṇas</s> are not the <s>pramāṇas</s> of anything whatsoever. // NagVvy_41

children.text: atha matam apekṣya siddhis teṣām ity atra bhavati ko doṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: If, then, you think: 'Their establishment depends [on objects]' — what fault is there in that?

children.text: siddhasya sādhanaṃ syān nāsiddho 'pekṣate hy anyat || NagVvy_42
children.translated_text: That would be proving what is already established, for what is not [yet] established does not depend on anything else. // NagVvy_42

children.text: sidhyanti hi prameyāṇy apekṣya yadi sarvathā pramāṇāni |
children.translated_text: If <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) are established only in dependence on <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge),

children.text: bhavati prameyasiddhir nāpekṣyaiva pramāṇāni || NagVvy_43
children.translated_text: then the establishment of <s>prameyas</s> occurs without depending on <s>pramāṇas</s> at all. // NagVvy_43

children.text: yadi ca prameyasiddhir nāpekṣyaiva bhavati pramāṇāni |
children.translated_text: And if the establishment of <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) occurs without depending on <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge),

children.text: kiṃ te pramāṇasiddhyā tāni yadarthaṃ prasiddhaṃ tat || NagVvy_44
children.translated_text: what need have you for the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s>? That for whose sake [they exist] is already established. // NagVvy_44

children.text: atha tu pramāṇasiddhir bhavaty apekṣyaiva te prameyāṇi |
children.translated_text: If, however, the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) depends indeed on <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge),

children.text: vyatyaya evaṃ sati te dhruvaṃ pramāṇaprameyāṇām || NagVvy_45
children.translated_text: then there is certainly a reversal for you of <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>prameyas</s>. // NagVvy_45

children.text: atha te pramāṇasiddhyā prameyasiddhiḥ prameyasiddhyā ca |
children.translated_text: If, for you, the establishment of <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) is through the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s>, and

children.text: bhavati pramāṇasiddhir nāsty ubhayasyāpi te siddhiḥ || NagVvy_46
children.translated_text: the establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> is through the establishment of <s>prameyas</s>, neither of the two is established for you. // NagVvy_46

children.text: sidhyanti hi pramāṇair yadi prameyāṇi tāni tair eva |
children.translated_text: If <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) are established by <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), and those same [<s>pramāṇas</s>]

children.text: sādhyāni ca prameyais tāni kathaṃ sādhayiṣyanti || NagVvy_47
children.translated_text: are to be established by <s>prameyas</s>, how will those [<s>prameyas</s>] establish them? // NagVvy_47

children.text: sidhyanti ca prameyair yadi pramāṇāni tāni tair eva |
children.translated_text: And if <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) are established by <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge), and those same [<s>prameyas</s>]

children.text: sādhyāni ca pramāṇais tāni kathaṃ sādhayiṣyanti || NagVvy_48
children.translated_text: are to be established by <s>pramāṇas</s>, how will those [<s>pramāṇas</s>] establish them? // NagVvy_48

children.text: pitrā yady utpādyaḥ putro yadi tena caiva putreṇa |
children.translated_text: If a son is to be produced by a father, and if by that very son

children.text: utpādyaḥ sa yadi pitā vada tatrotpādayati kaḥ kam || NagVvy_49
children.translated_text: the father is to be produced, then tell: in that case, who produces whom? // NagVvy_49

children.text: kaś ca pitā kaḥ putras tatra tvaṃ brūhi tāv ubhāv api ca |
children.translated_text: And who is the father and who is the son there? Tell about both of them,

children.text: pitṛputralakṣaṇadharau yato bhavati no 'tra saṃdehaḥ || NagVvy_50
children.translated_text: who bear the defining characteristics of father and son, for there is no doubt about this. // NagVvy_50

children.text: naiva svataḥ prasiddhir na parasparataḥ parapramāṇair vā |
children.translated_text: The establishment of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) is neither self-derived, nor from each other, nor from other <s>pramāṇas</s>,

children.text: na bhavati na ca prameyair na cāpy akasmāt pramāṇānāṃ || NagVvy_51
children.translated_text: nor from <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge), nor without any cause at all. // NagVvy_51

children.text: kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmāvasthāvido bruvīran yat |
children.translated_text: Those who know the states of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) would say that

children.text: kuśalaṃ svabhāvam evaṃ pravibhāgenābhidheyaḥ syāt || NagVvy_52
children.translated_text: the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of wholesome [dharmas] is wholesome; thus it should be designated by way of classification. // NagVvy_52

children.text: yadi ca pratīya kuśalaḥ svabhāva utpadyate sa kuśalānām |
children.translated_text: And if the wholesome <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) arises dependently for wholesome

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ parabhāvaḥ svabhāva evaṃ kathaṃ bhavati || NagVvy_53
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), that would be <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature); how then can it be <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature)? // NagVvy_53

children.text: atha na pratītya kiṃ cit svabhāva utpadyate sa kuśalānām |
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) arises for wholesome

children.text: dharmāṇam evaṃ syād vāso na brahmacaryasya || NagVvy_54
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) without depending on anything, then there would be no dwelling in the holy life. // NagVvy_54

children.text: nādharmo dharmo vā saṃvyavahārāś ca laukikā na syuḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) nor <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) would exist, and worldly conventions would not exist;

children.text: nityāś ca sasvabhāvāḥ syur nityatvād ahetumataḥ || NagVvy_55
children.translated_text: and things with <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) would be permanent; being permanent, they would be without cause. // NagVvy_55

children.text: evam akuśaleṣv avyākṛteṣu nairyāṇikādiṣu ca doṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Likewise, the same fault applies to unwholesome, indeterminate, conducive-to-liberation [dharmas] and so on;

children.text: tasmāt sarvaṃ saṃskṛtam asaṃskṛtaṃ te bhavaty eva || NagVvy_56
children.translated_text: therefore, all conditioned and unconditioned [dharmas] would follow for you. // NagVvy_56

children.text: yaḥ sadbhūtaṃ nāmātra brūyāt sasvabhāva ity evam |
children.translated_text: One who would say that here a name is real and possesses <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature)—

children.text: bhavatā prativaktavyo nāma brūmaś ca na vayaṃ sat || NagVvy_57
children.translated_text: that must be answered by you; we do not say a name is real. // NagVvy_57

children.text: nāmāsad iti ca yad idaṃ tat kiṃ nu sato bhavaty utāpy asataḥ |
children.translated_text: And as for this [claim] that 'a name is unreal,' does it belong to what exists or to what does not exist?

children.text: yadi hi sato yady asato dvidhāpi te hīyate vādaḥ || NagVvy_58
children.translated_text: Whether of the existent or the non-existent, in both ways your argument is defeated. // NagVvy_58

children.text: sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ śūnyatvaṃ copapāditaṃ pūrvam |
children.translated_text: The emptiness of all things has been established previously;

children.text: sa upālambhas tasmād bhavaty ayaṃ cāpratijñāyāḥ || NagVvy_59
children.translated_text: therefore, this reproach is against a thesis that has not been asserted. // NagVvy_59

children.text: atha vidyate svabhāvaḥ sa ca dharmāṇāṃ na vidyata itīdam |
children.translated_text: Now, if <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) exists but does not belong to <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena)—this

children.text: āśaṅkitaṃ yad uktaṃ bhavaty anāśaṅkitaṃ tac ca || NagVvy_60
children.translated_text: objection that was raised becomes groundless. // NagVvy_60

children.text: sata eva pratiṣedho yadi śūnyatvaṃ nanu prasiddham idam |
children.translated_text: If negation is only of what exists, is not this <s>śūnyatva</s> (emptiness) already established?

children.text: pratiṣedhayate hi bhavān bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvam || NagVvy_61
children.translated_text: For you negate the lack of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of things. // NagVvy_61

children.text: pratiṣedhayase 'tha tvaṃ śūnyatvaṃ tac ca nāsti śūnyatvam |
children.translated_text: If you then negate emptiness, and that emptiness does not exist,

children.text: pratiṣedhaḥ sata iti te nanv eṣa vihīyate vādaḥ || NagVvy_62
children.translated_text: then your thesis that negation is of what exists is itself defeated. // NagVvy_62

children.text: pratiṣedhayāmi nāhaṃ kiṃ cit pratiṣedhyam asti na ca kiṃ cit |
children.translated_text: I do not negate anything, nor is there anything whatsoever to be negated;

children.text: tasmāt pratiṣedhayasīty adhilaya eṣa tvayā kriyate || NagVvy_63
children.translated_text: therefore, when you say 'you negate,' you make a false charge against me. // NagVvy_63

children.text: yac cāharte vacanād asataḥ pratiṣedhavacanasiddhir iti |
children.translated_text: And as for what I said—that the negating statement regarding the non-existent is accomplished through speech—

children.text: atra jñāpayate vāg asad iti tan na pratinihanti || NagVvy_64
children.translated_text: here, speech makes known that 'it is non-existent'; it does not annihilate it. // NagVvy_64

children.text: mṛgatṛṣṇādṛṣṭānte yaḥ punar uktas tvayā mahāṃś carcaḥ |
children.translated_text: As for the great objection you raised again regarding the mirage example,

children.text: tatrāpi nirṇayaṃ śṛṇu yathā sa dṛṣṭānta upapannaḥ || NagVvy_65
children.translated_text: hear the determination on that too—how that example is appropriate. // NagVvy_65

children.text: sa yadi svabhāvataḥ syād grāho na syāt pratītya saṃbhūtaḥ |
children.translated_text: If that grasping existed by its own nature, it would not arise dependently;

children.text: yaś ca pratītya bhavati grāho nanu śūnyatā saiva || NagVvy_66
children.translated_text: and that which arises dependently—is that not itself <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)? // NagVvy_66

children.text: yadi ca svabhāvataḥ syād grāhaḥ kas taṃ nivartayed grāham |
children.translated_text: If grasping existed by its own nature, who could turn back that grasping?

children.text: śeṣeṣv apy eṣa viddhis tasmād eṣo 'nupālambhaḥ || NagVvy_67
children.translated_text: Know that the same applies to the rest; therefore, this is <s>anupālambha</s> (non-apprehension). // NagVvy_67

children.text: etena hetvabhāvaḥ pratyuktaḥ pūrvam eva sa samatvāt |
children.translated_text: By this, the absence of reason has been answered, as before, due to the same [argument];

children.text: mṛgatṛṣṇādṛṣṭāntavyāvṛttividhau ya uktaḥ prāk || NagVvy_68
children.translated_text: which was stated previously in the procedure of refuting the mirage example. // NagVvy_68

children.text: yas traikālye hetuḥ pratyuktaḥ pūrvam eva sa samatvāt |
children.translated_text: The reason regarding the three times has been answered previously, due to the same [argument];

children.text: traikālyapratihetuś ca śūnyatāvādināṃ prāptaḥ || NagVvy_69
children.translated_text: and the counter-reason regarding the three times is obtained by the proponents of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). // NagVvy_69

children.text: prabhavati ca śūnyateyaṃ yasya prabhavanti tasya sarvārthāḥ |
children.translated_text: For whom this <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is possible, for him all purposes are possible;

children.text: prabhavati na tasya kiṃ cin na prabhavati śūnyatā yasya || NagVvy_70
children.translated_text: for whom <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is not possible, nothing whatsoever is possible for him. // NagVvy_70

children.text: yaḥ śūnyatāṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ madhyamāṃ pratipadaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: He who declared <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way)

children.text: ekārthāṃ nijagāda praṇamāmi tam apratimabuddham || NagVvy_71
children.translated_text: to be of one meaning—I bow to that incomparable <s>Buddha</s>. // NagVvy_71
